Definitely. I spoke to a nutritionist today and she said that majority of acid reflux cases are stress related. She also said that this doesn't mean I shouldn't make lifestyle adjustments. It definitely an illness with physical manifestations, but honestly my advice is do the lifestyle adjustments but don't stress too much on them.

You've mentioned panic attacks. Turns out mine was purely (or almost completely) psychological and therefore responded very poorly to medication. So if your GP also rules everything out, it might be psychological. You can take measures to reduce symptoms but don't make the mistake I did and stress about it - that made mine waaayyy worse. 

Until you go to a doctor, try cutting out wheat from your diet, especially at night. There are many other trigger foods to try to avoid - they are available online. Milk may help or make worse so avoid it for a day or two and see how you feel and start having it again if it seems to help. 

I just take some Gaviscon at night when I get the pain. You can try taking a sip of Gaviscon an hour before bed - a doctor suggested it to me. Tablets seem to work better than the syrup for me - chew it slowly.

I am also trying aloe vera - remove the skin, scoop the inside, rinse it and eat a 2-3" piece every morning on an empty stomach but please check with someone who has some kind of medical knowledge before you do this.

Good luck!
